title: Stained Glass Panel with Lead Line Editor
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive stained glass panel editor with lead line (came) editing capabilities.

## Scene Setup
- Use an OrthographicCamera looking straight at the XY plane (z-forward). Frustum sized so the panel spans roughly 8x10 world units centered at origin.
- Background color: #1a1a2e (dark blue-grey, like a dim cathedral interior).
- Add a DirectionalLight from (2, 3, 5) with intensity 1.2 and a soft AmbientLight at intensity 0.3.
- Place a large backlight plane (PointLight or emissive plane) behind the glass panel at z = -1 to simulate sunlight streaming through, color #fff8e0, intensity 2.0.

## Stained Glass Panel
- Create a rectangular panel frame (8 wide x 10 tall) using dark grey MeshStandardMaterial (metalness 0.8, roughness 0.3) as a thin border (0.3 units thick).
- The panel interior is divided into an initial grid of 6 glass panes (2 columns x 3 rows). Each pane is a PlaneGeometry with MeshPhysicalMaterial: transmission = 0.85, thickness = 0.15, roughness = 0.1, ior = 1.5. Assign each pane a random saturated color from this palette: ['#c0392b','#2980b9','#27ae60','#f39c12','#8e44ad','#e74c3c','#1abc9c','#d35400'].
- Between each pane, render lead lines (cames) as thin rectangular meshes (width 0.12 units) with MeshStandardMaterial color #2c3e50, metalness 0.9, roughness 0.4.

## Lead Line Editor
- The user can add new lead lines to subdivide existing panes. Clicking on a glass pane selects it (highlight with a subtle emissive glow, emissive intensity 0.3). The selected pane index is tracked.
- Press 'H' to split the selected pane horizontally (into top/bottom halves). Press 'V' to split the selected pane vertically (into left/right halves). Each split creates a new lead line and two new panes replacing the old one. The new panes get random colors from the palette.
- Press 'D' to delete the last-added lead line (undo last split), restoring the previous pane.
- Maximum total panes allowed: 24. If at max, splits are rejected.

## Color Picker
- When a pane is selected, pressing 'C' cycles its color to the next color in the palette array.
- Add a DOM overlay HUD at top-left showing: 'Panes: {count} | Leads: {count} | Selected: {index or none}'.
- Add a button with id 'btn-reset' that resets the panel to the initial 6-pane grid.

## Light Angle Control
- Press ArrowLeft / ArrowRight to rotate the backlight position around the Z axis in 15-degree increments (orbiting behind the panel at radius 5). This changes how light filters through the colored glass. Track the angle in degrees (start at 0).

## Transparency Control
- Press ArrowUp / ArrowDown to increase/decrease the global transmission value of ALL glass panes by 0.05 per press, clamped to [0.3, 1.0]. This simulates frosted vs clear glass.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- paneCount: number of current glass panes
- leadCount: number of current lead line meshes
- selectedPaneIndex: index of selected pane or -1 if none
- selectedPaneColor: hex string of selected pane color or null
- globalTransmission: current transmission value (number, 2 decimal precision)
- lightAngleDeg: current backlight angle in degrees
- splitHistory: array of split records [{type:'H'|'V', paneIndex: number}]
- maxPanesReached: boolean, true if paneCount >= 24
- lastAction: string describing last action ('split_h', 'split_v', 'undo', 'color_cycle', 'reset', 'light_rotate', 'transmission_change', 'select', 'none')
- paneColors: array of hex color strings for all current panes
- frameCount: integer incremented each animation frame

Ensure all materials and meshes are properly created. Use requestAnimationFrame loop. The page must be fully self-contained in one HTML file.
physics_constraints: Transmission values must be clamped to [0.3, 1.0]. Light angle wraps at 360 degrees. Pane count must never exceed 24. Split undo must restore exact previous state. Total pane area should remain constant after splits (conservation of area). Lead count = initial_leads + number_of_splits_performed.
